children: RIYADH —Saudi Arabia’s operating revenue index recorded 4.9 percent year-on-year increase in July 2026 compared to the same month in 2025. The index also registered a 1.2 percent monthly increase compared to June 2026, according to the short-term business indicators for July 2026 released by the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT).

The preliminary results indicated that the annual growth in operating revenues was supported by a 13.5 percent increase in manufacturing activities, a 9 percent increase in financial and insurance activities, a 6.5 percent increase in information and communication activities, a 1.6 percent increase in construction activities, and a 0.8 percent increase in wholesale and retail trade and vehicle repair activities.

On a monthly basis, operating revenues in mining and quarrying activities increased by 6.4 percent, followed by information and communication activities at 3.7 percent, manufacturing at 0.8 percent, accommodation and food services at 0.6 percent, and construction at 0.1 percent.

The workers’ compensation index rose by 7.4 percent year-on-year, driven by growth in manufacturing (10.3 percent), wholesale and retail trade and motor vehicle repair (6.2 percent), financial and insurance activities (6.4 percent), construction (4.6 percent), and mining and quarrying (2.7 percent).

On a monthly basis, workers’ compensation index increased by 0.3 percent, with growth recorded in human health and social work (2.6 percent), information and communication (1.8 percent), transport and storage (0.8 percent), mining and quarrying (0.3 percent), and financial and insurance activities (0.1 percent).

Regarding construction activity, the number of building permits issued increased by 4.4 percent year-on-year, reaching 5,828 permits in July 2026, compared to 5,582 permits in July 2025. The number of permits also recorded monthly growth of 15.5 percent, compared to 5,045 permits issued in June 2026.

The authority indicated that short-term business statistics aim to measure the performance of various economic sectors through monthly indicators that monitor developments and growth rates across all economic activities of establishments operating in the business sector.

title: ZAWYA: Saudi Arabia’s operating revenues rise 4.9% in July 2026
